headline: Earnings slip despite record purchase volume and buybacks
summary_short: Synchrony's Q2 2026 net earnings fell 8.5% y/y to $885M even as diluted EPS rose 3.6% y/y to $2.59 on heavy buybacks; purchase volume hit a record $49.8B, up 8% y/y.
summary_long: Net earnings fell 8.5% y/y to $885M as a 5% rise in provision for credit losses (smaller reserve release: $163M vs $265M a year ago) and 7% higher other expense (operational losses, technology investment) outpaced 2% net interest income growth. Diluted EPS still rose 3.6% y/y to $2.59 because weighted-average diluted shares fell 11.9% y/y on $850M of quarterly buybacks. Purchase volume hit a record $49.8B (+8%), loan receivables grew 2% to $102.2B, and net interest margin expanded 30bp to 15.08%, though efficiency ratio rose 170bp to 35.8%. Estimated CET1 fell to 13.2% from 14.2% (partly a capitalized-software presentation recast). No new forward guidance was issued in the release.

drivers.explanation: Net interest income rose 2% on lower interest-bearing liability costs from falling benchmark rates, partly offset by lower liquidity-portfolio and loan yields; interest and fees on loans rose 1% on higher average receivables.
Provision for credit losses rose 5% on a smaller loss-reserve release ($163M vs $265M a year ago); other expense rose 7% on higher operational losses and technology spend, outpacing revenue growth.
EPS rose even as net income fell because weighted-average diluted shares dropped 11.9% y/y, reflecting $850M of buybacks this quarter alone.
CEO cited strong new-account growth, active accounts inflecting back to growth, and record purchase volume across all five sales platforms as evidence of momentum despite the y/y earnings decline.
